column1: # Where each woven Old English plural in lex-ang.tsv was read.
# A noun row weaves its second form under an English plural, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. Each modern plural has named
# the headword line that prints it since 2026-10-08; an Old English headword
# line prints no plural, but English Wiktionary declines every Old English
# noun in a table whose cells carry a class per slot. On 2026-10-08 every
# woven plural was read in the rendered table (action=render) of its entry:
# the cell classed nom|p, the nominative plural, quoted as the table prints
# it with every form the cell holds, "nominative plural frīend, frēond,
# frēondas". tests/tools/ang-forms.test.ts fails on a plural changed in one
# file and not the other, a line citing an entry its gloss was not read in, a
# quote from another cell or not printing its plural, and a line outliving
# A page holding more than one word of a spelling is read by sense: the
# table under the etymology whose definitions give the gloss — lagu, the law,
# "laga, lage", not the sea's "laga"; hund, the dog, "hundas", not the
# hundred's "hund" — and where one etymology declines a noun in two genders,
# the table of the gender ang-genders.tsv gives it: hyll, m, "hyllas", not the
# feminine "hylla, hylle"; clāð, m, "clāðas", not the neuter "clāð".
# One source per line, the one the quote is from:
#                      (the title drops macrons and the dots of ċ and ġ)
#   wright:§<n>        Joseph and Elizabeth Mary Wright, Old English Grammar
#                      (Oxford, 2nd ed., 1914), the section that prints the
#                      form; archive.org, oldenglishgramma00wrig. Read in the
#                      page images, not the text, whose OCR drops every macron
#                      and reads "pl." as "pi.". Wright prints no dots on ċ
#                      and ġ, so a quote of his is read with the pack's set
#                      The quote opens with the entry's head as the
#                      dictionary prints it, then " … " and the passage that
#                      prints the form. Its acute accents are read as the
#                      pack's macrons, a long diphthong's moved from its
#                      second vowel to its first (treów is trēow), its
#                      hyphens dropped and the pack's dots set aside. The
#                      head must spell the headword and,
#                      for a noun, name the gender the row has, since one
#                      spelling can head two entries: "treów, es; n." is the
# A wikt: source is always an entry ang-glosses.tsv read the row's gloss
# in, so the two ledgers cannot choose different words of one spelling; a
# bt: line shows which word it read by the head it quotes. Where the gloss was
# read in two, a ð spelling's page and the þ page it names, the line cites
# the one whose table prints the woven form as the pack spells it.
# Two things the pack writes otherwise than the tables, on every word, are
# read as one: ð, which the pack keeps where a teaching edition prints it and
# Wiktionary files under þ, and the doubled palatal, which the pack writes
# cg, "dg" in its pronunciation key, where the tables write ċġ.
# Eight woven plurals cite Wright. Six are forms the tables do not print:
# water's and head's, "wæter" and "hēafodu", from his paradigm (§ 347),
# which a note calls older than the tables' "wætru" and "hēafdu"; setl's,
# "setlu beside setl" (§ 349); mete's "mettas" (§ 386), where the table
# prints "metas"; winter's "wintru beside winter" (§ 397); and burg's
# "byrig beside byrg" (§ 220). Path's gloss was read in Bosworth–Toller
# alone, and § 54 prints "the plural forms paþas, paþa, paþum". And sister's
# Two cite Bosworth–Toller. Family's gloss was read there, and its entry
# quotes "Ealle híwscipas þeóda". The tree's table prints "trēowu", and
# Wright § 363 declines trēo(w) like cnēo, whose plural is cnēo (§ 361) — a
# paradigm, which implies the form and does not print it — and the neuter
# treów of Bosworth–Toller quotes "and óþre treów", other trees, beside
# Four were wrong. "roads" was woven weġas, a dot before a back vowel,
# where the table prints "wegas" and Wright § 320 "pl. dagas, days; wegas,
# ways", the guttural; it is wegas now. "sisters" was woven sweostru, which
# neither the table, whose plural is the collective ġesweostor, nor Wright
# prints: his paradigm gives the plural as "sweostor" (§ 415), where
# brōþor, mōdor and dohtor take -ru beside it, so it is sweostor now. And
# "floors" was woven flōras, a masculine plural, under a row ang-genders.tsv
# calls feminine, as Wiktionary does and Bosworth–Toller first ("f: flór,
# es; m."); a row's gender is printed under both its forms, so it is the
# table's feminine "flōra" now. And "dreams" was woven swefn, like its
# singular, where the table prints "swefnu" and Bosworth–Toller's swefen
# quotes "Swefnu gefremminge habbaþ, dreams will have accomplishment"; it
# One is an adjective's. Stranger's entry, fremde, is the adjective's, and
# Wiktionary gives it no noun section; its table declines it strong and weak,
# in cells classed str|nom|m|p and wk|nom|m|p rather than nom|p, which is why
# it was first queued as having no table. Its line quotes the weak cell of
# its gender, "weak masculine nominative plural fremdan", the form woven, and
# ADJECTIVE in tests/tools/ang-forms.test.ts names it for the test to read
# the nominative plural of the row's gender, strong or weak.
# Two were their headwords' dots. Soldier's and key's tables print "cempan"
# and "cǣġa, cǣġe", with a bare c, and Wright §309 keeps Germanic k a
# guttural before the umlauts of the back vowels, §310 listing "cempa,
# warrior" with cēpan and cyning; so the headwords are cempa and cǣġ since
# 2026-10-09, their cards following through RENAMED, and their lines quote
# Church's was its second c. The pack wove ċirican, the second c the
# guttural before -an, and the table prints "ċiriċan"; Bülbring,
# Altenglisches Elementarbuch (1902), § 499 Anm. 4, read in the page image,
# prints the West Saxon plural "ćirićean 'Kirchen'", both c palatal, the e
# marking the second before a back vowel, as in the pack's own tǣċan. So
# churches is ċiriċan since 2026-10-25, and its line quotes the cell.
# 7 woven plurals are not here, because the table of their entry prints
# another form and no grammar read yet prints the woven one, or their entry
# has no table, or their gloss was read in Bosworth–Toller alone: QUEUED in
# tests/tools/ang-forms.test.ts names each with what its table prints, until
